'''Christopher P. McKay''' (born 1954)<ref name='"jpl"'>{{cite web |url=https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.cgi?orb=1;sstr=5382 |title=5382 McKay (1991 JR2) |website=ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/|access-date=2 March 2021 |quote=McKay. Discovered 1991 May 8 by R.H.McNaugth at Siding Spring. Named for Christopher P. McKay (b. 1954), sapce scientist and exobiologist&nbsp;...}}</ref> is an American [[planetary science|planetary scientist]] at [[NASA Ames Research Center]], studying [[atmosphere|planetary atmospheres]], [[astrobiology]], and [[terraforming]].  McKay majored in [[physics]] at [[Florida Atlantic University]], where he also studied mechanical engineering, graduating in 1975.<ref>Edward Silverman, "[http://www.the-scientist.com/?articles.view/articleNo/12124/title/Scientists--Paths-To-Eminence--What-Are-The-Turning-Points-/ Scientists' Paths To Eminence: What Are The Turning Points?]", ''The Scientist'', Vol:6, #2, 20 January 1992.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Christopher McKay {{!}} Academic Influence |url=https://academicinfluence.com/people/christopher-mckay |access-date=2022-07-20 |website=academicinfluence.com |language=en}}</ref> He also received his PhD in [[wiktionary:astrogeophysics|astrogeophysics]] from the [[University of Colorado at Boulder|University of Colorado]] in 1982.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080916051905/http://quest.nasa.gov/projects/spacewardbound/atacama2006/bios/Chris_McKay.html Chris McKay Planetary Scientist - NASA Quest]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://humbleapproach.templeton.org/Many_Worlds/ |title=Many Worlds Symposium |access-date=2012-08-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121029003330/http://humbleapproach.templeton.org/Many_Worlds/ |archive-date=2012-10-29 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mckay |url=https://spacegrant.org/programs/service-award/mckay/ |access-date=2022-07-20 |website=National Space Grant Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Career==
McKay has done research on planetary atmospheres, particularly the atmospheres of [[Titan (moon)|Titan]]<ref>e.g. [http://www.sciencemag.org/cgi/content/abstract/275/5300/642 Photochemically Driven Collapse of Titan's Atmosphere], Ralph D. Lorenz, Christopher P. McKay, and Jonathan I. Lunine, ''Science'', Vol. 275 pp. 642–644, 31 Jan. 1997</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Christopher McKay |url=https://www.sciencefriday.com/person/christopher-mckay/ |access-date=2022-07-20 |website=Science Friday |language=en-US}}</ref> and [[Mars]], and on the origin and evolution of life.<ref>[http://www.sciencemag.org/cgi/content/abstract/276/5311/390 Organic Synthesis in Experimental Impact Shocks], Christopher P. McKay and William J. Borucki, ''Science'', Vo. 276 pp. 390–392, 18 April 1997</ref> He is a co-investigator on the [[Huygens probe]], the [[Mars Phoenix]] lander, and the [[Mars Science Laboratory]]. He also performed field research on [[extremophiles]], in such locations as [[Death Valley]], the [[Atacama Desert]],<ref>[http://www.sciencemag.org/cgi/content/full/306/5700/1289c Microbial Life in the Atacama Desert], R. M. Maier, K. P. Drees, J. W. Neilson, D. A. Henderson, J. Quade, J. L. Betancourt;, Rafael Navarro-Gonzalez, Fred A. Rainey, and Christopher P. McKay, ''Science'', Vol. 306 pp. 1289–1290, 19 November 2004</ref> [[Axel Heiberg Island]], and ice-covered lakes in [[Antarctica]]. McKay is the Principal Investigator of the proposed [[Icebreaker Life]] astrobiology mission to Mars.<ref name='Icebreaker2018'>{{cite journal | title = The ''Icebreaker Life'' Mission to Mars: A Search for Biomolecular Evidence for Life | journal = Astrobiology | date = April 5, 2013 | author = Christopher P. McKay  |author2=Carol R. Stoker |author3=Brian J. Glass |author4=Arwen I. Davé |author5=Alfonso F. Davila |author6=Jennifer L. Heldmann |author7=Margarita M. Marinova |author8=Alberto G. Fairen |author9=Richard C. Quinn |author10=Kris A. Zacny |author11=Gale Paulsen |author12=Peter H. Smith |author13=Victor Parro |author14=Dale T. Andersen |author15=Michael H. Hecht |author16=Denis Lacelle |author17=Wayne H. Pollard | s2cid = 21073805 | volume = 13 | issue = 4 | pages = 334–353 | doi = 10.1089/ast.2012.0878 | pmid=23560417|bibcode = 2013AsBio..13..334M }}</ref> In 2015 he received the [[Nevada Medal]].

He was a member of the board of directors of the [[Planetary Society]] and also works with the [[Mars Society]], and has written and spoken on [[space exploration]] and terraforming.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Haynes | first1 = R. H. | last2 = McKay | first2 = C. P. | year = 1992 | title = The Implantation of Life on Mars: Feasibility and Motivation | journal = Adv. Space Res. | volume = 12 | issue = 4| pages = 133–140 | doi=10.1016/0273-1177(92)90167-v| pmid = 11538133 |bibcode = 1992AdSpR..12d.133H }}</ref><ref>C. P. McKay and M. M. Marinova, "The Physics, Biology and Environmental Ethics of Making Mars Habitable", ''Astrobiology''  1, 89–109 (2001).</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Marinova | first1 = M. M. | last2 = McKay | first2 = C. P. | last3 = Hashimoto | first3 = H. | year = 2005 | title = Radiative-Convective Model of Warming Mars using Artificial Super-Greenhouse Gases | url = https://zenodo.org/record/895737| journal = J. Geophys. Res. | volume = 110 | issue = E3 | page = E03002 | doi = 10.1029/2004JE002306 | bibcode=2005JGRE..110.3002M| doi-access = free }}</ref> He is also an adviser for the Microbes Mind Forum.<ref>[http://microbes-mind.net/advisers.html Microbes Mind Forum – Advisors] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228170953/http://microbes-mind.net/advisers.html |date=2014-02-28 }} 
(2014)</ref>

==Ethics of terraforming==
McKay advocates a moderately [[biocentrism (ethics)|biocentric]] position in the [[ethics of terraforming]], arguing that we must thoroughly explore a planet such as [[Mars]] first to discover whether there is any microbial life before taking first steps toward terraforming, and that if indigenous alien life is found in an obscure niche or dormant on Mars, we should remove all Earth life and alter Mars to support the global spread of this alien life on Mars.<ref>C. P. McKay, "Let's Put Martian Life First", ''The Planetary Report'', XXI(4), 4–5 (2001).</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=McKay|first1=Chris|title=Planetary Ecosynthesis on Mars: Restoration Ecology and Environmental Ethics|url=http://esseacourses.strategies.org/EcosynthesisMcKay2008ReviewAAAS.pdf|date=December 2007|access-date=2017-01-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200401190045/https://esseacourses.strategies.org/EcosynthesisMcKay2008ReviewAAAS.pdf|archive-date=2020-04-01|url-status=dead}}</ref>  He has held a series of public debates with [[Robert Zubrin]], who advocates a moderately [[Anthropocentrism|anthropocentric]] position on the ethics of terraforming.<ref>C. P. McKay and R. M. Zubrin, "Do Indigenous Martian Bacteria have Precedence over Human Exploration?" in ''On to Mars: Colonizing a New World'' (pp. 177–182)</ref><ref>R. M. Zubrin and C. P. McKay, "A World for the Winning: The Exploration and Terraforming of Mars", ''The Planetary Report'', XII(5), 16–19 (1992).</ref>
